query: Across role, grade level, and subject, which open-response themes are associated with satisfaction?

per_column.name: teaching_approach
per_column.rationale: External pedagogical variable extracted from open responses with well-separated, interpretable categories (lecture, project-based, flipped, etc.) that can be segmented and compared against satisfaction. Distribution is reasonably spread.

per_column.name: innovative_curriculum_adaptation
per_column.rationale: Ordinal three-level scale (high/moderate/minimal) that is interpretable and well-balanced, enabling meaningful grouping against satisfaction. Associational to the theme of adaptation rather than a restatement of satisfaction.

per_column.name: student_engagement_level
per_column.rationale: Clear three-way engagement categories with good spread; a plausible correlate of satisfaction distinct from it, supporting interpretable segmentation.

per_column.name: subject_remote_fit
per_column.rationale: Well-separated fit categories (high/moderate/low) that provide an associational, interpretable dimension to compare against satisfaction across subjects.

per_column.name: instructor_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Interpretable ordinal responsiveness levels usable for grouping; borders on being a near-proxy of satisfaction, but responsiveness is a distinct external theme. Some NULLs but categories remain comparable.

judge.rationale: All five added columns are external, associational themes derived from the open responses, each with a small number of interpretable, well-separated categories that can be grouped and cross-tabulated against satisfaction as well as role, grade level, and subject. None merely restates satisfaction, and none is so fine-grained or near-constant as to preclude comparison. instructor_responsiveness and student_engagement_level trend close to satisfaction conceptually, but remain distinct explorable dimensions. As a set they strongly support discovering interpretable relationships with the focus.
